title: Pooling & Hierarchical Feature Learning
description: Downsample feature maps with Max Pooling and Average Pooling. Understand translation invariance and receptive fields.

slides.title: Compressing Spatial Information 📉
slides.content:
# Pooling Layers

As representations progress deeper through a CNN, we progressively decrease spatial dimensions $(H, W)$ while expanding channel depth $(C)$. This is accomplished using **Pooling Layers**.

### The Purpose of Pooling:
1. **Reduces Parameter Count & Compute:** Shrinking spatial dimensions cuts memory footprint for subsequent layers.
2. **Translation Invariance:** A slight shift in pixel coordinates (e.g. 1 pixel left) yields the identical maximum activation.
3. **Expands Receptive Field:** Deeper neurons perceive progressively larger chunks of the original input canvas.

slides.title: Comparing Pooling Operations ⚖️
slides.content:
# Max Pooling vs Average Pooling

| Pooling Method | Operation | Key Benefit | Typical Placement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Max Pooling ($2 \times 2$, Stride 2)** | Extracts maximum value in each $2 \times 2$ window | Retains sharpest, most salient edge/feature activations | Intermediate layers throughout CNN backbone |
| **Average Pooling ($2 \times 2$)** | Computes arithmetic mean across window | Smooth feature aggregation; softer downsampling | Less common in intermediate stages |
| **Global Average Pooling (GAP)** | Averages entire feature map $(H \times W)$ to a single scalar | Eliminates dense FC layers; drastically suppresses overfitting | Final layer right before Softmax classifier |

quizData.question: What is the primary architectural advantage of Global Average Pooling (GAP) at the output of modern CNNs compared to traditional flattened fully connected layers?

options.text: It eliminates millions of dense weights that cause severe overfitting
It increases the spatial resolution of the image by 4x
It forces all weights to become binary step functions
It doubles the required GPU VRAM

quizData.explanation: Global Average Pooling computes the average of each feature map directly into class logits, removing millions of parameters and preventing overfitting.

slides.title: Max Pooling in PyTorch 🐍
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Feature map: batch=1, channels=16, height=28, width=28
feat_map = torch.randn(1, 16, 28, 28)

# Standard 2x2 max pool with stride 2
pool = nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2)
downsampled = pool(feat_map)

print('Before pooling shape:', feat_map.shape)
print('After pooling shape: ', downsampled.shape) # 14x14
